result.note: Tested concrete outcomes of Modi's February 2026 Israel visit: labour mobility, agri and cyber centres, and UPI launch.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, India and Israel signed 27 agreements during Prime Minister Modi's visit to Israel. Consider the following statements about the outcomes:
items: India will send 50,000 workers to Israel over five years.
An India-Israel Centre of Excellence in Cybersecurity will be established in Israel.
The Centres of Excellence network for transferring Israeli agri-technologies will expand to 100 hubs.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The India-Israel Centre of Excellence in Cybersecurity will be set up in India, not Israel. The labour deal addresses shortages in Israel's construction and nursing sectors, and a Villages of Excellence initiative will take agri-technologies to the grassroots.
questions.source: An India-Israel Centre of Excellence in Cybersecurity will be established in India to facilitate cooperation on cybersecurity, an area where Israel has established itself as a global leader.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, which Indian payment system, described as the world's largest real-time payment system, was announced to launch in Israel?
questions.explain: UPI is launching in Israel, allowing Indian tourists and businesses to pay via QR code. This lets them bypass Western credit card networks.
questions.source: India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI), the world's largest real-time payment system, is launching in Israel.
